review_text:
Pleasantly surprised and happy with the product. I was (admittedly) apprehensive about buying the Halo after reading the reviews here and on Cnet but have been pleasantly surprised by the product. I've been using them for a good part of the day to listen to music and take conference calls from my PC..it fits my head just fine without any issue (I must have the Jabra "standard" head shape!). Sound is okay for work listening and the folks on the other end of my VoIP calls have reported normal voice quality.

***UPDATED*** I'm now a few weeks on of daily use and continue to be happy with the Halo!

PROS
* The touch volume slider is convenient and reasonably sensitive - not a selling point but it works.
* Sound quality - not too bassy or trebl-y. These do a reasonable job of blocking out ambient "office noise"
* Voice quality - I've used these on Skype and my mobile and folks on the other end still report good quality

CONS
* The inner headphone lining does tend to grab a bit of fuzz (a minor annoyance)

review_text: They'll break in a year or less. I got my Halo at a Best Buy about a year ago. What a waste of a Benjamin for a headset to function properly for less than a year. They won't work with the PS3, either.

review_text: Great design. I bought these headphones after seeing my friend's pair. They're very aesthetically appealing (very subtle when you're wearing them and I've gotten a few compliments about how they look). There are also several common sense additions which make me happy. Firstly, they charge via an included micro usb cord, instead of a proprietary charger. Secondly, there is no obnoxious blinking blue light on at all times (like the Samsung SBH170). Thirdly, folding the headset up turns it off, and unfolding it turns it back on (and autosyncs). The interface is easy to figure out, although the double-tap to skip tracks feature is a little touchy. One thing to be careful of: the length of the headphones is adjustable, but not the curvature, so if you have a small head, the fit might be a little loose. Overall, I highly recommend this product. If you've never had bluetooth headphones before, it's great and this is a quality pair.

review_text:
Third time's a charm. edit 1/26/16: I couldn't resist the feeling like I gave up on them too soon so I ordered directly from v-moda a white crossfade wireless. I'm going through a second trial. Really loving them so far. Comparing them to my m100 the bass is definitely tighter and in bluetooth mode there's almost more bass. I really prefer the refinements of this sound wired or wireless to the original m100. I still love the m100, but those have gone to my wife and these are mine now. In my original review I mentioned some hiss/sizzle - it turns out these headphones are so clear that they make some recordings' flaws completely apparent. Yes, in low volume there is a bluetooth hiss, but at high volume what I was hearing on many tracks was hiss in the recording. I a/b this back and forth with the m100 and cfw in wired mode and the hiss was there at high volumes. Don't get me wrong, maxed out there might be hiss from the internal amp being pushed, but that's to be expected on any device with its volume maxed. I'm really enjoying them this time around, I have one more headphone to try out but its $550 from master and dynamic - and at that price point it better sound twice as good as these, because if it doesn't i'm sticking with v-moda. I'm leaving my old review up just for comparison's sake. Still leaving it at four stars because theres no 4.5 option. They make my temple and jaw sore after a while in normal use, and almost instantly when lying down. Also, I thougth cliq fold being omitted would be an issue but honestly the carrying case is form fitting and fits in my gym bag just as easily. Its not as short, but its flatter than the m100 case. Plus I found myself not folding my m100 because the earpads would get squished and began to flatten out prematurely. I had to order replacements.

The V-Moda Crossfade wireless is difficult for me to review because ultimately I returned it and kept the m100. The two I received had battle scars from shipping. Both were sealed with the vmoda red ribbon and had the stickers over the earcups so i'm presuming they were brand new. However the first one had scratches on the silver trim between the earcup and earpad. The replacement had a scuff on the earcup and the microphone had shifted in its housing. If you looked inside the pinhole you could see the mic warped to the left. I think there was insufficient packing material in the box and it was bouncing around. Thats not VModas fault. So none of this reflects my rating. Just letting people know to inspect their expensive new toys! Now for the rating.

I loved the wired sound, and really liked the wireless sound. Wired it is very reminiscent of the m100 with slightly tighter bass, and slightly less of it too. Its gives a sense of a more balanced sound than the m100. It is pretty much V-moda sound signature just refined slightly. If you don't A/B them you wouldn't know there's a difference.

Wireless was great unless you turned the volume on the headphone itself up past half, Then there would be this distortion/sizzle/hiss at the top end of the sound regardless of how low the volume was on the music player. Up past half, to me - is where the amp really drove the headphones and made the bass thump, but that's where the sizzle lived. It was hard for me to find a balance between player/headphone volume. The bluetooth was also not dead quiet. I don't listen to music very loudly so I could always hear the signal noise. Its not a "bluetooth" thing in the sense that not every device suffers from this, but I've encountered it before. I have a bluetooth dongle right next to me that doesn't have this line level hiss at all. This was my ultimate reason for not replacing it another time after the second dud. I got my m100 for half the cost of the CFW; I wasn't going to pay double when the main feature was not up to standard. I believe they are almost there. If there's a CFW 2.0 Val will probably address all the signal quality issues with bluetooth. Until then i'm sticking with wired m100.

Minor concerns of mine were the battery life over time (year two and up), sweat/rain damaging the electronics, and falls. The physical build quality is as durable as the m100 but the electronics add more variables that could fail in the event of a minor fall/spill. I know people use bluetooth on the go,so if you're on a train and they fall or it starts to rain, would the destruction be covered under warranty? Too scary for me to take that change.

so why 4 stars? They're excellent headphones wired, if you find the balance in volumes they're very good in wireless mode. I can be objective enough to know that something is good even though its not good for me in particular.

review_text: Poor quality these days. I've been buying Sony earbuds for at least 10 years. In fact, I still have a pair that I bought more than 6 years ago and they work great. I got a new pair of Sony earbuds as the wires on the old ones started to get stiff when I was outside in the cold weather (sound quality still great). So I set aside my old earbuds as backup and started using the new ones. A few months later, one ear quit working. I chided myself for not being more careful handling them and bought a new pair, same model. I was super careful with them, always carefully coiled them up and put them back in my pocket after each use. Two months later, one ear quit working. So I packaged up my warranty and sent the headphones to the Sony warranty fulfillment center, with a letter explaining that I love Sony earbuds and was hoping they can help. That was six months ago and I never heard back. I have to say that it is now time to explore other brands. Too bad!

review_text:
Really nice stereo headphones. I just got a imac and wanted bluetooth stereo headphones or headset to use with my imac and my ipad.
Do not care about cell phone use, just wanted a nice stereo wireless set for music and movies.
This Jabra Halo set is PERFECT!!! Most everyone else was suggesting the motorola S9 set. So I tried that first.
One word for the motorola S9..AWFUL!!! Had a terrible time pairing to my iMac. But worse, the S9 is heavy, bulky
and really unconfortable to wear. They drove me nutz. Could not stand that heavy tight wrap-around behind the head
on the S9. If you laid back in a chair, the S9 poked into my neck and really was so unconfortable..PERIOD.
So I returned them and got the Jabra Halo BT650s. About the only other option in wireless headsets for stereo and music use.
Well. the halo set is soooo light weight. Like draping a scarf over your head. You don't feel it at all.
No.. I guess I would not run or exercise with them because of the fit is not pressure tight (a good thing).
BUT.. if you want a bluetooth great sound stereo headset, that easily paired to my iMac first try (unlike the motorola S9),
then this is the set to get.
I can not believe how good they feel on the head/ears. You could wear these all day and never have an issue.
Where the S9 gave me neck cramps after a few minutes. Like having popcorn stuck in your teeth, the motorola S9 drove me crazy.
The Jabra is like a draped scarf draped over your head. So nice!!!
And the sound is NOT too loud. Easily adjustable. Also, if using on a imac, in the iMac bluetooth settings you can further
adjust the volume there too, if needed.
Like I said, I do not use them for a cell phone or running/jogging. But for pc/mac use they are the only solution.
Great sound. Great fit. Great pairing. Great job Jabra..!

positive_points: easily paired to iMac on the first try

aspect_sentiments.evidence: easily paired to my iMac first try
You could wear these all day and never have an issue.
sound is NOT too loud. Easily adjustable.

review_text:
Superb headphones!. So why am I giving headphones that I consider to be fantastic only 3 stars? Because I also happen to own the Plantronics Backbeat pros. Those headphones are superior in almost every way for the same price or far less if you get the older version.

I will focus first on these headphones and then the comparison to the Plantronics. The Crossfades scream quality and beauty when unboxing. The materials are the highest quality and they just feel good. The metal construction is top notch and the plastics are solid and substantial. The metal accent shields are beautiful and just make the headphones look good.

Controls are sparse, but effective. There is a power/pairing button on the bottom of the right headphone that functions well and is fairly intuitive. At the top are a series of three button. The center one pauses/starts the music and answers calls. The two surrounding it control volume and skip music forward or backward.

These headphones are very comfortable. I have a large head and they accommodate me with ease and I don't have too much discomfort even after a couple of hours use. They are even more comfortable after adding the XL pads. The pads make the ear opening larger and put more distance between the ear and the speaker. The XL pads are so much better that I think VMODA should have made them standard instead of selling them as an extra. Especially at this price point.

Sound. If I hadn't heard a better set, I would have been completely happy with this headphone. Bass is good and highs are where they should be. Mids are a bit too recessed for my taste so some vocals are lost. They play well at low volumes and can get plenty loud. Sound bleed is minimal and the outside world does not intrude too much. In the end, these really are great sounding headphones. Again, the XL pads improve the sound greatly. They provide a greater depth of sound and a much warmer tone.

This brings me to the reason that I am returning these and why they are only receiving 3 stars from me, despite how much I like them. I happen to own the Plantronics Backbeat Pro and they are superior to the Crossfades in nearly every way. The controls are more intuitive and easier to use. The Plantronics have APTx, active noise cancelling, voice prompts, and longer battery life. Most importantly, they simply sound better. As good as the Crossfades are, the Backbeats are better. Deeper bass, better mids, and they sound far clearer than the Crossfades. The Crossfades are very muddy by comparison. The Vmodas are constructed of better quality materials, are lighter, and look better, but that is not enough to justify buying them when a better alternative exists. Especially since you can get the old version of the Plantronics for far less.

To sum up. Great headphones that you will likely be really happy with, but there are better available for similar or less money. I also think that it is a sin that VMODA charges extra for the XL pads which are a necessity to get the best out of them. I really wanted to keep these and be happily ever after, but I simply can't. Back they go.

review_text:
Bass to Bust your Brain and Adequate Sound Quality for a lower tier price. The Bass Booster is for when you show your friends how much of a douche you truly are (half the reason I bought them), or you just really really feel like self inflicting a migraine headache. the sound quality is alright, about worth what you would pay for them, maybe the quality of some other brands costing $99+ but nothing special, The booster only hits at the top most bass frequencies, so its no Hanz Zimmer theater experience. What is special is how they fit (at least my head) snug as a glove. My best headset is my desk headphones $200 Turtle Beach with Dolby 7.1. Haven't found much better audio inside of the sub $300 mark, the problem is that I cannot use the Turtle Beaches around the house because they're quite large and loose on my head (much stiffer when new), but these Crushers suit me quite well for every day use away from the desk with an Adequate level of quality.

Side note that I owned a pair of the SkullCrushers in 11' and if I remember correctly they had a much better Bass frequency, didn't give spontaneous migraine headaches, and fit about the same as the Crushers with much more storing flexibility. Although they did lack in sound quality as these feel a bit crisper and more lively. I would still recommend the SkullCrushers to people who want to experience a ripe sub woofing right into their ear canals as opposed to the cerebral jack hammering the new Crushers give out.

review_text:
Good headphones. Above average sound and build quality.
Bought these based on reviews that said they were almost as good as the Bose equivalent models (but cheaper). Sound quality is very good. With the noise cancelling on the sound quality reduces slightly along with an increase in bass and volume. There is a low level hissing sound with Noise Cancelling turned on, however it's not too annoying and wouldn't be noticeable in a noisy environment such as a plane anyway.
The Noise Cancelling is very effective at reducing constant noise like jet engines. Other sounds are reduced but not entirely (takes the edge of them). As these are "over ear" headphones (like earmuffs) they passively reduce outside noise anyway. Your ears can get warm as they are fully enclosed within the headphones muffs, but are comfortable.
Comes in handy tuff zip case with enough room for an iPod Classic and USB cable. Various adapters are included as standard with the headphones.

review_text:
Good, but hot. As many others have said, the sound is great and the fit, though a bit tight for my big head, is comfortable. The main problem is that it does make my head sweaty. Granted, I'm a bit hot-blooded and sweat easily, but the warmth of these headphones worries me because I live in Japan and walk/take the train to work. Once it starts getting hot here, I'm worried my headphones will be exceedingly uncomfortable.

That being said, there aren't too many options and I tried the Motorola ones on. They were super uncomfortable, right from the get go.

I've had a few range problems as well, with the sound cutting out when the iPhone was in my pants pocket, although that seemed to go away or lessen with time. Weird.

One cool thing: the battery ran out yesterday and I pulled out the extra cord that came with the headphones and was able to use them without the Bluetooth functioning. Meaning, if you're on a long flight or can't recharge for a while, if you carry this cord with you you'll still be able to use the headphones.

By the way, I recommend Poddities ([..]) as a convenient way to carry your iPhone around your neck, especially helpful for commuters who walk/ride to work.

review_text:
Took them right back for a refund. Let me start be stating that the audio quality was acceptable, both for calls and music, but overall, the design is seriously lacking in the following respects:

1. The power switch is integrated into the headband hinge -a snap open, fold-and-slide affair that feels rather insubstantial and twice collapsed (inadvertently shutting down the radio) while in the process of taking the unit off my head.

2. Beyond the power switch functionality, the folding configuration provides no significant space savings. It's not as though collapsing these headphones will make them any less bulky in a laptop bag or purse.

3. The earpieces do not pivot or swivel at all -basically, if your head isn't a perfect fit (and mine isn't), they don't sit right on your ears and constanly slide off.

4. The software-based, touch sensitive volume control is a profoundly unreliable, counterintuitive gimmick. A hardware dial or rocker switch would have been much better.

5. The headband and earpieces are lined with some kind of synthetic velour that traps lint and fuzz admirably, but doesn't add to the comfort. And finally,

6. You can't control the tracks on an iPod Touch or iPhone 3G/3Gs with it. I know that's not Jabra's fault -that is a problem with Apple's current version of A2DP, so I don't consider it a knock on this product per se. I just mention it for the benefit of anyone planning to use these with one of those devices.

If you're really in love with the aesthetics of this unit, consider the Jaybird Sportsband. They're $10 cheaper, and they have basically the same features, but the earpieces adjust to the shape of your cabeza and you get real, tactile controls.

review_text:
Took them right back for a refund. Let me start be stating that the audio quality was acceptable, both for calls and music, but overall, the design is seriously lacking in the following respects:

1. The power switch is integrated into the headband hinge -a snap open, fold-and-slide affair that feels rather insubstantial and twice collapsed (inadvertently shutting down the radio) while in the process of taking the unit off my head.

2. Beyond the power switch functionality, the folding configuration provides no significant space savings. It's not as though collapsing these headphones will make them any less bulky in a laptop bag or purse.

3. The earpieces do not pivot or swivel at all -basically, if your head isn't a perfect fit (and mine isn't), they don't sit right on your ears and constanly slide off.

4. The software-based, touch sensitive volume control is a profoundly unreliable, counterintuitive gimmick. A hardware dial or rocker switch would have been much better.

5. The headband and earpieces are lined with some kind of synthetic velour that traps lint and fuzz admirably, but doesn't add to the comfort. And finally,

6. You can't control the tracks on an iPod Touch or iPhone 3G/3Gs with it. I know that's not Jabra's fault -that is a problem with Apple's current version of A2DP, so I don't consider it a knock on this product per se. I just mention it for the benefit of anyone planning to use these with one of those devices.

If you're really in love with the aesthetics of this unit, consider the Jaybird Sportsband. They're $10 cheaper, and they have basically the same features, but the earpieces adjust to the shape of your cabeza and you get real, tactile controls.

review_text: Never without a backup pair. I'm wearing the 3rd pair of these and have just ordered a 4th (just in case). Gave them 4 stars only because I find the connection at my iPhone wears out, causing distortion and then silence. I keep buying them because they're the only headphones I've found that have the controls on the cord and stay in my ears. I wear hearing aids, and these fit in the ear canal sufficiently to work around the speakers in the aids, and ear buds don't, nor do the buds stay in my ears without the hearing aids. I just wish that connection were more secure and the wire at the connection more substantial (it actually cracked in the last pair after less than a year). Something strange is going on with the volume controls for the iPhone 3Gs, too. The controls work perfectly for listening to Audible books, but not at all for phone calls. This started less than a week after opening the newest pair of headphones. I'd like to know of another brand as good in other respects; would pay more if they'd last longer.

review_text:
Great sound quality and fit, but broke after 2 months of normal use. Company sent replacement. I ordered these in February of this year, when they were 79.99. I love the sound quality and the fit. Unfortunately, they broke within the first two months of use. I contacted the seller and am waiting on their response. I will update my review as things get sorted out. Like I said, I love everything about these earbuds, but I want them to last longer than two months of normal use.

UPDATE: Was called as I requested by a treblabs customer service representative. They are sending a replacement set promptly. I will update to 4 or 5 stars after I receive the product, because like I said I love using these earbuds. The original problem was that they out of nowhere would no longer hold a charge or turn on, so keep my story in mind when purchasing. It could be something to do with the battery dying and not being able to recharge. However, I love using these earbuds so I will have high hopes about this replacement.

review_text:
Buyer beware... I usually don't leave reviews unless I can remain positive for the most part but I really feel like I need to voice my opinion about this product. I am one of those people who think they can read all the negative reviews and then think it will be better for me because I am really good with this stuff. I was dead wrong.

I have wanted a pair of these for a very long time now but after only a week with these things I have had nothing but problems,

-Half the 'felt' from the headband is already falling off. It's all over my head every night and very annoying and makes the product look terribly cheap.

-The cheesy fold to power off/ power on is a complete joke and the hinges feel extremely fragile to me and likely to last less than a few months at most. This means there is no way to wear them around your neck if out and about with no other way to hold them and wish to have them turned off. And it also means you have to fold them in order to charge with out interfering with your backup bluetooth headset. I found this to be a very annoying problem becuase I wanted to avoid hinging them as much as possible because of the cheap hinge feel.

-The charging indicator works nothing like advised in the manual. You plug it in and the battery blinks red for 2 hours and then just turns off. It never turns to green like it is supposed to and unless it does it wont turn on. The first charge took over 4 hours, 2 hours blinking red and then turned green after another 2 hours of no indication light at all. The second charge I had it plugged in for 5 hours, it blinked red for the first 2 hours and then did nothing for the next 3 hours and when I went to use them the battery was still dead!

-Terrible, uncomfortable fit that will have your ears throbbing within the hour and a design that in no way attempts to stay flat against your ears or stay even remotely positioned on your head in an active environment.

-Constant clicking and static sounds heard during silent periods between songs/during pause time.

-It is not possible to initiate voice commands with the headset. Long pressing the center button only puts it in pairing mode to pair with multiple devices at the same time. Seriously a bluetooth hands free headset that cannot initiate voice commands so I can make a call?

-Jabras customer support declined to respond to my emails or call me despite their *STOP DO NOT RETURN TO STORE* labeling. I gave them a fair chance to support their product and they declined.

+On the bright side when they did work the phone calls were crystal clear and music sounded amazing with deep rich lows and crisp vibrant highs with plenty of volume even when working in noisy environments with power tools. No call complaints what so ever.

+Volume controls worked very well, precise and consistent for me. EVEN with my work gloves on.

Promptly returned. BUYER BEWARE.

The JayBird Sportsband is a far superior product in almost every way. [[ASIN:B003TO52A2 JayBird Sportsband Bluetooth Headphones (Midnight Black)]]

review_text: Product was not "NEW" as claimed. I had purchased a HALO headset a few months ago from Sprint and really love it. The sound quality is unbelievable for such a thin headset. I wanted to get another one to give away as a Xmas present and decided to purchase it on-line to save some money. Because I was going to give as a gift I needed it to be in the orignal unopened Jabra retail packaging. The product I ordered was listed as "NEW" by this seller. However, what I got was a refurbished unit that came came in a zip-lock bag inside a plain white box. The user guide looked like a cheap fake compared to the one I got from Sprint. And here's what really convinced me, the warranty insert was titled "LIMITED WARRANTY REFURBISHED PRODUCTS". I should have been suspicious that the price was so much lower than Amazon's. In the future I will only buy from them.

review_text:
Design Flaws Destroy its Value. The Jabra HALO is a very nice looking set of headphones. The sound quality is fine (I'm not picky though), but there are a number of design flaws that really make it a no-buy for me.

1. The only way to turn the headphones on and off is by folding in their right side. The power mechanism is built into the hinge. For someone who does a lot of on-and-off listening, it's really annoying to not be able to just turn the headphones off.

2. The folding arms are weak. After about a month of regular use, small cracks started to form around the hinges where the headphones fold. Now, after about three months, shards of plastic are constantly splitting off, and the hinges no longer stay open on their own. I have to carefully put the headphones on, and then the pressure from resting against my head keeps them in place. A moving part like this should have been designed to withstand much more wear and tear.

3. The touch-sensitive area on the right earpiece that does volume and next/previous track is terrible. It is sluggish and slow to respond. You'll also find that you accidentally change the volume a lot of the time when you're trying to reach the play/pause button, or trying to change tracks. Using a touch sensor here is pure gimmick, I would definitely prefer physical buttons.

4. If you have glasses, you'll be miserable. The headphones, although sleek, are really uncomfortable to wear for more than a few minutes if you're wearing glasses.

If these headphones cost $10.00, I wouldn't mind just buying a new pair every couple of months, but at over $50.00 I can't recommend them.

review_text: Tangled. The sound quality is decent and I can't complain for the price and if rating on sound quality alone I would give it at least 4 star. The thing that's really annoying about these is that the cord becomes tangled constantly. It sticks to itself when you're using them and if you don't carefully put them away every time you end up with a tangled knot. As it is I always have to carefully put them away and pull them out when I want to use them which is something that I have never experienced to this degree with other products. I also prefer a plug jack that's at a 90 degree vs. the straight out that these have as it allows a smaller profile for my ipod which is important when it's strapped to my arm at the gym.

review_text: Best ear buds I have owned. I prefer to use over the ear headphones. I usually find ear buds to be uncomfortable, especially the ipod head phones. These head phones are very comfortable, I hardly notice they are there. Of course the most important factor in headphones is how they sound and that is where these really shine. They sound great for all types of music, a very clear and sophisticated sound, they are less over bass heavy which is an issue I had with the cheaper skull candy headphones I have owned. The noise isolation works well to improve the sound as well. The construction is also very high quality withe metal volume adjuster and rubber coated braided cable. Be careful on this last point however, I purposely bought the older style which are the ones I am reviewing, the newer version looks cheaper with plastic pieces and a rubber cable. All around I am very happy with my purchase, well worth the money.

The second pair is still kicking but I was just tired of constantly pushing the buds back into my ears. I did burn the overmold of the 1/8" connector on the exhaust of my motorcycle and they kept working. Durabiblity is really not the issue here. There are just more comfortable and convenient products for the same price or less. Try the MEE M6 product.

review_text:
A refined M-100 with wireless capabilities? Oh yes!. V-Moda is a brand that has always been very fashion forward. It was until the M80 and M100 in which they were able take traction and gain popularity by merging their designs with respectable acoustics that was generally pleasing to a wide range of people. Now, they have finally taken what made them popular and removed the wires. This is the new Crossfade Wireless.

The box is a bit taller than the M100’s version because there is no longer the click fold hinge that allowed the headphone to collapse in upon self, rendering the new Crossfade wireless not as portable. This may be a deal breaker to some, but the included case is still of quality and attempts to minimize its footprint by molding its shape to the headphone. Included in the box is a spare set of shields usually this will be the custom set you’ve created. You have your quick guide and warranty information especially informing you about V-Moda’s kick ass immortal life program. Inside the specially molded clamshell zipper case you’ll find the micro USB cable to charge your headphones and the 1 button with an in-line microphone cable allowing you to use the Crossfade wireless in passive mode in the event the battery dies or you simply yearn for the best possibly sound quality. And at last you have the clip to mount the case on a bag or your belt.

The Crossfade Wireless retains the same incredibly rugged and sexy design as the M-100 and LP series. What’s even more amazing is that it keeps the same size even despite now housing internal electronics to allow wireless connectivity. I have the XL pads installed and these offer improved cushion depth, a bigger soundstage and a smoother sound as well a wider ear diameter for superior comfort over the stock pads. A much recommended upgrade. The headband offers substantial padding to avoid hot points at the top of the head and remains aesthetically pleasing by not being overly bulky and/or not aligning to the curvature of your head. In summary, these are gorgeous, well-built headphones that can easily withstand everyday wear and tear and if you do break them, the immortal life program is an option.
The location of the wireless controls are fairly intuitive. On the top left we have the volume down button. On the top middle, we have the multi button, play, pause, answer and reject calls as well as activating your voice assistant and on the top right we have the volume up button. Moving down we have a single rocker that when pushed to the middle turns on the headphone and pairs it to the last known device and when pushed and held to the far right for 2-3 seconds puts it in pairing mode. The Crossfade wireless can be connected to 2 devices at once, for example a smart watch and a smart phone or a smart phone and a tablet.

The M-100 was at a time my favorite headphone, but it was until I ventured off into what other high quality portable offerings were available that made me see its flaws. The M-100 is undeniably a pleasing and fun sounding headphone with stunning bass performance, but its resolution and coherency leaved some to be desired. The Crossfade Wireless is a welcoming improvement. By taking the famous M-100 sound and fine tuning the frequency response balance to be more linear as well as brining out more resolving power to allow the subtle textures and harmonic low level details to surface has resulted in being my favorite Bluetooth headphone, period and possibly being my overall “favorite” sounding headphone surpassing the Master & Dynamic MH40. Yes, these are that DAMN good. When in Bluetooth operation, the following said about the sound quality of the Crossfade Wireless is still mostly the same, but it just doesn’t have the same level of detail and overall focus as when it is wired and plugged into a fine setup. Other than that, these are the best sounding Bluetooth headphones I have heard and owned surpassing the Parrot Zik 2, Sennheiser Momentum Wireless, Sony XB950BT, Bang & Olufsen H8, Definitive Technology Symphony 1, Beats Studio Wireless, Beats Solo2 Wireless, Samsung Level Over and Bowers & Wilkins P5 Wireless. The sound of Crossfade wireless is still immediately on the fun sounding side of the spectrum, but still very refined and coherent. No part of the frequency range is absent.

The bass extends endlessly and punches you with no mercy when the song calls for it. This is one of the most downright seductive bass presentations that I have ever heard and it manages to integrate into the midrange quite stupendously well without destroying that whole octave. The midrange is still a bit relaxed, but it’s more neutral sounding than the M100 and sounds clean and proportionally well represented. Vocals sound rich and full even whilst the bass is turning the skin on your face into water waves. The treble seems a bit more present and extended over the M100, but most importantly, it’s a cleaner and more natural sounding treble which really helps clean up the initial transients thus improving imaging and granting the Crossfade Wireless a very, very good soundstage for a closed back and among my best performers in that region.

Now, these aren’t my best sounding portables, but they are not far from it whilst retaining a character that grants them undeniable enjoy ability. I love to be able hear every single thing in the recording, but I more importantly enjoy feeling the emotion in the recording more and this is where the Crossfade Wireless excels.

review_text:
Excellent music audio, average phone audio. I've owned many Bluetooth headsets, mainly because I'm very hard on them. I have several hours of commuter train rides each working day and any Bluetooth headset I buy will get constant usage. I bought a Jabra Halo about three months ago and so far, I'm extremely happy with this product.

There are several thing I really like about the Halo:

1) They fit my head very well, snug but comfy. The problem is, not everyone has my head's dimensions but for me, they're perfect.
2) Audio quality for music is excellent..much better than the Plantronics/Altec-Lansing Backbeat headphones I was previously using. Specifically, the bass response is much better and the mid range sounds have much more punch.
3) These headphones are able to connect to more than one device at a time, two at a time to be precise. Hence, I can switch from my iPhone, laptop or iPad without explicitly disconnecting from one unit and reattaching to another. This is an extremely convenient and helpful feature.
4) The Jabra Halo connects much more quickly and with less fuss than any other Bluetooth headset I've owned. Other Bluetooth headsets seemed to connect sometimes but not others, and invariably, I end up fiddling with them, turning them off and on, turning the Bluetooth functions on the source device off and on..etc..etc to get a stable connection. The Halo connects just about every time on the first shot to all my devices.
5) The quality of materials is high and feels substantial.

About the only thing I don't think is truly excellent about the Jabra Halo is the phone functions. While the headset works decently with my iPhone, it's not as amazing as it's stereo audio performance for music. The Halo works but it's preyty average where the phone calls are concerned. Hence, I give the Jabra Halo only four stars but that's much more out of consideration of the needs of others than my own.

Indeed, I like this product so much that I just ordered a second set, which I'll keep on my shelf in case my first unit fails. As I said, I use my Bluetooth headphones heavily and eventually, they will die..no reason to think that day is coming soon however, when it does arrive, I'm going to want another set of these headphones. Jabra might discontinue them and replace them with something worse and hence, my second set are an insurance policy against future screwups on the company's part. For right now, these are the best Bluetooth headphones I've found..and I've had a few.

review_text:
It's a little difficult, but I'm keeping mine. I've shopped around and tried out SOOOO many different stereo bluetooth devices. Most notably have been devices by Motorola and Plantronics. The specific model numbers elude me at the moment. The Motorola was nice, but cumbersome and the battery died after a few months. It had a band that went behind the head and was inflexible making it very uncomfortable to wear while leaning my head against anything such as the headrest in the car, or a pillow in bed. The Plantronics faired better, but the noise canceling wasn't very good.

I typically use my devices for conversations of both a business as well as a personal nature. For talking with my friends it would suffice, but not for clients. I also use my device when I'm working out at the Gym. It doesn't do very well when I work up a sweat, but the Halo device fares better than others.

I had a great deal of difficulty pairing this device the first time and it took me 3 days worth of emails with the technical support department of Jabra. They wouldn't provide me with a phone number and usually returned my emails within a few hours. I still can't figure out how to move forward or backwards through my music. I did it once by accident, and haven't been able to figure it out since.

Overall, the noise canceling is good, and the quality of the sound it produces is very good as well. The only reason I'm not ranking this more than 3 stars is because of how difficult it was to figure out, and the fact that I STILL can't get certain functions to work. Overall, I like this better than other products of this kind.

review_text: Great sound for a great value!!!. I know the wired headphones are "old news" by now but I got these because I'm going on a long plane trip soon and didn't want to pay $350 for "decent" ones. Well, I was certainly skeptical. I put these on and was blown away especially for the price!!! LOVE! I listen to all kinds of music and while I haven't had the opp to watch a video with them, I doubt they will disappoint. These mothas rock!! And yeah..for the bass heads..they vibrate your drums. If you're tired of wussy headphones with all highs and little to no mid or bass, these are for you! Bass turns down easily with a slide bar. I'm sure when I'm stuck on a plane with all the annoying noises, these will help. And I wore them a bit for like 3-4 hours so far..very comfortable. I used the Bose ones a while back. Can't comment on the new Bose vs "everything else out there" but for the money, you can't go wrong! Loved them so much I got my brother a pair the same day I tried my new ones out just because they really are that great, especially for the cost. I'd pay almost twice as much. AND they do fold up,which is great. Hell yeah. Boom. Love.

I put these on and was blown away especially for the price!!! LOVE! I listen to all kinds of music and while I haven't had the opp to watch a video with them, I doubt they will disappoint. These mothas rock!! And yeah..for the bass heads..they vibrate your drums. If you're tired of wussy headphones with all highs and little to no mid or bass, these are for you! Bass turns down easily with a slide bar. I'm sure when I'm stuck on a plane with all the annoying noises, these will help. And I wore them a bit for like 3-4 hours so far..very comfortable. I used the Bose ones a while back. Can't comment on the new Bose vs "everything else out there" but for the money, you can't go wrong! Loved them so much I got my brother a pair the same day I tried my new ones out just because they really are that great, especially for the cost. I'd pay almost twice as much. AND they do fold up,which is great. Hell yeah. Boom. Love.

review_text:
Product is too fragile. I bought this in January to replace wired headsets for my iPhone, and it worked very well. I read all the reviews about flimsy hinges and the indicator lights not working as described, and yes - they are correct. However, even though the indicator lights do not do what the manual says, I had no trouble charging or pairing it to the iPhone. It stayed paired for weeks at a time, and only once in a while did I need to have the iPhone "forget" it and start over. The hinges thing is bad - I eventually stopped closing the left hinge, but the right hinge has to be closed to turn it off. If you are extremely careful about pulling the hinge out before folding, it might last a little longer.

The call quality on phone calls was excellent and worked flawlessly from audio to call. Volume control was a little iffy because you can't see your right ear to know exactly where you are going to touch it - you might accidentally do something you didn't intend. But generally I had little trouble with volume.

I loved this headset - really - and I was as gentle as I could be with it. But eventually the right hinge lost a piece of plastic, even though it continued to work. The headset also loosened a little, so that it became harder to keep it over my ears. Then, last week, it stopped sending a bluetooth signal (which you can see as the blue indicator light). I imagine the connector wire is probably damaged, and I'm looking for my warranty info now. I won't be surprised if they say I damaged it, since that piece of plastic broke off, so I'm not hopeful they'll repair or replace it.

I give it 3 stars - I loved it and want to give it 5 but hey, it costs too much, especially for only 8 months of service. That being said, don't buy it - it's too fragile.

Average headphones only. I recently bought a different pair of Sony headphones from Amazon for under $10 [[ASIN:B0015AM38Q Sony MDR-ED12LP Earbuds (Silver)]]. They sounded so awesome for the price. Sadly, they were the hard kind of earbuds and just hurt my ears when I wore them. I was thrilled to see this $25 pair on sale Cyber Monday for only $15 and jumped on it after reading all the reviews here mentioning how great they were.

I have to admit, I am a bit disappointed. Not because they are bad headphones, they are not. However, they sound very average. The sound is pretty tinny, and the bass is nearly non existent. They are extremely comfortable, and that is why I will probably keep them. However, if sound quality is important to you, look elsewhere. These are simply average, and below the last two pairs I have had, both also under $30.

review_text:
I've got no strings on me!. I love running with over-ear headphones, and lately my Crossfade M-100s have been my go-to cans for that. The one thing that I've always hated while running with any headphones is dealing with the cords - pulling earbuds out of my ears, rubbing and getting in the way of arm movement with on-ear or over-ear, etc. I can tuck them in my shirt or whatever, but then they're annoying and pull when I turn my head. And let's be honest - most cordless headphones sound like garbage. Been there, done that, returned it. Yeah, first world problems but why not shoot for perfection? The only reason I even gave these a shot is because they're V-MODA and I'm not just surprised, I'm blown away.

V-MODA claims that these sound equivalent to wired headphones. I'm going to disagree for my most common use case - connected directly to my iPhone 6S. In this case, they sound a bit better. The integrated amplified delivers more and cleaner bass presence than my iPhone can. Not as good as with a standalone DAC/amp, but I'd say about 30% better than the iPhone alone - which is not a subtle improvement, and without the distortions introduced by the iPhone's electronic equalizer. You can practically see the strings on a bass guitar vibrating in your mind, and the bass drums have a beautiful kick. Highs and mids still feature V-MODA's trademark clarity and nice, even frequency response. So yes, the sound is wonderful, which is what everyone really cares about. I've seen some complaints in forums, but as far as I can tell these have been narrowed down to devices that just can't send good quality audio over Bluetooth. I haven't personally had any issues yet, but I've only tested with my iPhone and MacBook Pro. Charging is accomplished with a standard micro-USB cable, so most people won't have to worry about carrying extra cords or chargers to keep the Crossfade Wireless topped up while traveling. Battery life hasn't yet been an issue. They come with a typically excellent V-MODA travel case, the sort that puts every other brand to shame but V-MODA buyers have become pleasantly used to.

Minor quibbles:
* No cliq-fold hinges like the M-100s and XS. Sorry, V-MODA, you spoiled us and it's hard to go back.
* A single button for pause / resume / track-forward / track-back. I suck at pressing these fast enough, so I always wind up just pausing it.

I'm pretty nit-picky about things, so that's a pretty short list. I'm loving these so far!

review_text:
Average headphones only. I recently bought a different pair of Sony headphones from Amazon for under $10 [[ASIN:B0015AM38Q Sony MDR-ED12LP Earbuds (Silver)]]. They sounded so awesome for the price. Sadly, they were the hard kind of earbuds and just hurt my ears when I wore them. I was thrilled to see this $25 pair on sale Cyber Monday for only $15 and jumped on it after reading all the reviews here mentioning how great they were.

I have to admit, I am a bit disappointed. Not because they are bad headphones, they are not. However, they sound very average. The sound is pretty tinny, and the bass is nearly non existent. They are extremely comfortable, and that is why I will probably keep them. However, if sound quality is important to you, look elsewhere. These are simply average, and below the last two pairs I have had, both also under $30.

I bought them for my commuter train ride (1hr 30minutes) to drown out the noise and so they won't fall out of my ears (replacing iphone standard headphones). Once you have them in your ears correctly, you won't hear much else other than the music.

I am very happy with my purchase.

review_text: Durable and rockin'!. I returned my wimpy Sennheiser headphones to BB for some better quality headphones. I had heard nothing but good things about Skullcandy. After reading tons of reviews and testing out my dad's Skullcandy headphones, I was hooked. The great thing was that I was able to try the different kinds on before purchasing and these are my favorite in terms of comfort. I almost bought the Hesh2s, but the rounded ears hurt. I love the supraural earpieces and they are so comfy! The bass is INCREDIBLE! My mom thought they were great, too, and worthwhile in terms of noise-canceling even though this isn't an advertised feature. I also LOVE that they fold down to 40% and have a detachable cord because I've been through many Sony headphones where the cord pulled away from the earpieces. I'm very pleased with these and I recommend them highly! If I could change one thing it would be to make the cord longer, but I bought a 6 foot headphone extension cord at Walmart for less than $5 so it's not a huge problem!

negative_points: Cord is short

review_text:
Wouldn't stay put, dangerous sound blockage. I ordered these headphones for running, and 10 minutes into my run I had to just take them off and shove them in my pocket. They just would not stay in my ears, every time my jacket bumped into them even a little they popped right out of my ears. The only way I was able to fix it was by really shoving them into my ear canals, and then I could not hear a THING that was going on around me-- a city bus pulled up next to me without me ever realizing it was there. That is way too dangerous in my book, and I wish manufacturers would start making headphones that aren't a danger to runners and everyone around them!

About me: I'm a petite female with very small ears, and these felt like they were just a little too big still.

review_text: Better than I hoped. The sound quality is simply amazing for the price. I read the reviews about how great the bass is. It's even better than I imagined. It made my whole head vibrate. The sound is very clear even at high volume levels. The package I recieved does not come with the foam tips, but the silicon is very comfortable even after hours of wear, at least for me. review_text:
Pretty things don't always perform as expected!!. From the moment I first discovered these online I was in love with this sleek and stylish dream of a perfect headset. Unfortunately actually using them proved much more like a nightmare. While this headset is very visually stunning the performance leaves much to be desired. First and foremost, the headset does have a 30 foot range as advertised, but when you put it in your pocket (as I'm assuming that's where most people plan on putting their phones when they wish to utilize the features of a HANDS-FREE device) it constantly cuts in and out. I usually listen to calming music on my walk to and from school, but the constant blips make it even more frustrating than listening to the homeless people beg for change on the subway. It's a constant reminder of the very disc-man portable CD players that you had to stand stalk still with to use. My experience from the "noise canceling" microphone actually was the opposite, meaning the lovely people on the other end of my phone call could hear my cat breathing from the other side of the apartment!! Whoever wrote this description needs to get their hearing checked. Also IPHONE USERS BEWARE this device is not fully functionally with your iPhones!! The nifty volume control does work, but the track forward/back function is absent, it did however work with my Mac and is pretty nifty. As for the fit, the headset was constantly slipping off of my ears and onto my temples, which wouldn't be a problem if I could hear out of my temples. It would stay put on my head only when I was sitting still at home, but if I was trying to walk or turn my neck ever so slightly the headset would ride my silky smooth hair right off my head. The hinges that turned the device on/off felt very flimsy and kept bending the wrong direction!! YIKES!! Finally the battery life was not all it was cracked up to be, partially because the device would often stay on even when folded. Expect 6 hours period, not 6 hours of actual listening time. If I unplugged this device at 9 they would be dead by 3, only listening to music for the 20 min commute to and from campus. I encountered a stranger on the subway that had recently purchased and returned the Halo just the day before. He asked my humble opinion and completely agreed with almost every complaint.

In conclusion these are beautiful headphones and I received numerous compliments from friends, professors and complete strangers. Unfortunately I listen to music with my ears not my eyes and this experience was painful at best. I've said this about people for years and now I can easily apply it to this headset, when things are good to look at they don't have to perform as well because they're carried by their looks. Perhaps if these were made to function better I would repurchase them in the future, but for the time being I'm going to research a different model. :(

review_text:
Voodoo required. I bought this headset to pair with my Lenovo laptop. I work for a virtual company, so the bulk of our communications are on Skype and GoToMeeting. The headset "mostly" works. It can go days with no problems, but then it will indiscriminately disconnect and I just about have to kill a brindled calf in the pale moonlight to get it connected again. I'm not sure if it's a Bluetooth issue or a Jabra issue, but whatever the issue is, there is no hard and fast procedure for getting it to connect again. Sometimes it's just a matter of going through the re-connect procedure on the laptop, other times I have to fold the headset up, unfold it, then go through the re-connect process, still other times it requires a full restart of the computer to re-establish a connection. You can imagine this being a problem during an online meeting.

I have paired my Droid with out any reliability issues on this machine, so I'm fairly certain that my BT adapter is solid.

It's extremely frustrating when it doesn't work, so likely I'll be searching for a decent wireless USB solution. I was just hoping not to have to put another dongle on my computer.

Difficult and unpredictable reconnection process
Frustrating to use when connection fails

review_text:
One of the best pair of headphones iv'e heard to date. Take note that these are my first pair headphones that goes over $150 , so lets get started .

(BUILD QUALITY)
These headphones by far are the most durable pair of headphones iv'e ever owned and held, taken that they're $300 i wouldn't expect less ,just by holding them makes me feel like they can survive a three story drop to the ground and i bet they can . Everything from the headband down just screams quality in such a way that your money is being worth of and that applies to the sound as well, but we'll get into that in a bit.

(COMFORT)
All i can say is that these headphones are quite comfortable not the most comfortable iv'e tried but still to the average consumer they well very much find them satisfying to wear. No wearing fatigue at all overtime even though the clamping force is kinda strong, it makes me feel like they're telling me "i got you ", like they're never gonna let go and i like that in a way and it's all because of the headband , because of it's compact shape to give it a low profile it kinda conforms to your head and it really adds to the comfort ,but they will start to fall if you're head knocking like a possessed person to some heavy dubstep i can tell ya that . On to the ear pads , even though the ear pads are not too plush they're really comfortable ,but the comfort varies on the size of your ears , my experience with them is that my ears fit perfectly not too big or not too small and it has been great experience for me , my ears don't even touch the divers but that's just me , if you know that you're ears are big i suggest getting the XL pads i am myself are planning on purchasing them because who doesn't want 2X the comfort .

(BLUETOOTH CONNECTIVITY & BUTTON FUNCTIONALITY)
Not much to say here but when it comes to Bluetooth it's no joke, i can hardly tell the difference between when it's connected via Bluetooth or wired, yes it's that good and also they can go really far without braking up ,i can literally walk around some parts of my house with them on while my phone is in my room and nothing , i can say the max range can be up to about 50 feet or so . The buttons on these headphones i can say is that the placement is adequate and the feel of when you press on them are not really rouged but is enough to satisfy anyone. When it come to the functionality of the buttons it's really easy to operate [middle button : one tap = play/pause , two taps = skip track , three taps = previous track] and there's just the volume up and volume down, when using these buttons i find them very responsive but not too responsive where it's instant but over over all they're really good .

(SOUND QUALITY)
Now taken that these are my first headphones over $150 you'd expect me to say that these are the best iv'e heard and you're right ,the fidelity in this masterpiece of an headphone are insane , The highs are very present ,the mids are in a position where i can say that they are slightly less present but still has a strong influence and now the lows , i can say that they are as present as the mids but yet it doesn't distort the mids at all ,it actually blends with it really well also it's so strong that the headphone literally shake ,kinda like the sony pulse. Now on to the volume levels , i can tell ya that these headphones get way louder than the average headphone wired or non wired , when it's on Bluetooth mode the volume levels to me are way louder than wired ,that's because of the mini vamp inside the headphones to push that extra volume that normal Bluetooth headphones don't provide.

Ratings
BUILD QUALITY : 10/10
COMFORT : 7.5/10
BLUETOOTH : 10/10
BUTTON FUNCTIONALITY : 9/10
SOUND QUALITY: 10?10

OVERALL : 9.5/10

positive_points: High sound fidelity with strong lows and high maximum volume
negative_points: Headphones may start to fall off during heavy head movement

buttons on these headphones i can say is that the placement is adequate
the fidelity in this masterpiece of an headphone are insane

review_text:
Voodoo required. I bought this headset to pair with my Lenovo laptop. I work for a virtual company, so the bulk of our communications are on Skype and GoToMeeting. The headset "mostly" works. It can go days with no problems, but then it will indiscriminately disconnect and I just about have to kill a brindled calf in the pale moonlight to get it connected again. I'm not sure if it's a Bluetooth issue or a Jabra issue, but whatever the issue is, there is no hard and fast procedure for getting it to connect again. Sometimes it's just a matter of going through the re-connect procedure on the laptop, other times I have to fold the headset up, unfold it, then go through the re-connect process, still other times it requires a full restart of the computer to re-establish a connection. You can imagine this being a problem during an online meeting.

I have paired my Droid with out any reliability issues on this machine, so I'm fairly certain that my BT adapter is solid.

It's extremely frustrating when it doesn't work, so likely I'll be searching for a decent wireless USB solution. I was just hoping not to have to put another dongle on my computer.

review_text:
One of the best pair of headphones iv'e heard to date. Take note that these are my first pair headphones that goes over $150 , so lets get started .

(BUILD QUALITY)
These headphones by far are the most durable pair of headphones iv'e ever owned and held, taken that they're $300 i wouldn't expect less ,just by holding them makes me feel like they can survive a three story drop to the ground and i bet they can . Everything from the headband down just screams quality in such a way that your money is being worth of and that applies to the sound as well, but we'll get into that in a bit.

(COMFORT)
All i can say is that these headphones are quite comfortable not the most comfortable iv'e tried but still to the average consumer they well very much find them satisfying to wear. No wearing fatigue at all overtime even though the clamping force is kinda strong, it makes me feel like they're telling me "i got you ", like they're never gonna let go and i like that in a way and it's all because of the headband , because of it's compact shape to give it a low profile it kinda conforms to your head and it really adds to the comfort ,but they will start to fall if you're head knocking like a possessed person to some heavy dubstep i can tell ya that . On to the ear pads , even though the ear pads are not too plush they're really comfortable ,but the comfort varies on the size of your ears , my experience with them is that my ears fit perfectly not too big or not too small and it has been great experience for me , my ears don't even touch the divers but that's just me , if you know that you're ears are big i suggest getting the XL pads i am myself are planning on purchasing them because who doesn't want 2X the comfort .

(BLUETOOTH CONNECTIVITY & BUTTON FUNCTIONALITY)
Not much to say here but when it comes to Bluetooth it's no joke, i can hardly tell the difference between when it's connected via Bluetooth or wired, yes it's that good and also they can go really far without braking up ,i can literally walk around some parts of my house with them on while my phone is in my room and nothing , i can say the max range can be up to about 50 feet or so . The buttons on these headphones i can say is that the placement is adequate and the feel of when you press on them are not really rouged but is enough to satisfy anyone. When it come to the functionality of the buttons it's really easy to operate [middle button : one tap = play/pause , two taps = skip track , three taps = previous track] and there's just the volume up and volume down, when using these buttons i find them very responsive but not too responsive where it's instant but over over all they're really good .

(SOUND QUALITY)
Now taken that these are my first headphones over $150 you'd expect me to say that these are the best iv'e heard and you're right ,the fidelity in this masterpiece of an headphone are insane , The highs are very present ,the mids are in a position where i can say that they are slightly less present but still has a strong influence and now the lows , i can say that they are as present as the mids but yet it doesn't distort the mids at all ,it actually blends with it really well also it's so strong that the headphone literally shake ,kinda like the sony pulse. Now on to the volume levels , i can tell ya that these headphones get way louder than the average headphone wired or non wired , when it's on Bluetooth mode the volume levels to me are way louder than wired ,that's because of the mini vamp inside the headphones to push that extra volume that normal Bluetooth headphones don't provide.

Ratings
BUILD QUALITY : 10/10
COMFORT : 7.5/10
BLUETOOTH : 10/10
BUTTON FUNCTIONALITY : 9/10
SOUND QUALITY: 10?10

OVERALL : 9.5/10

review_text:
Probably the best bluetooth headphones out there so far, but not perfect yet. To be completely honest here, I'm a pretty big V-Moda fan when it comes to their crossfade line. I've owned the LP, the LP2, the M-100, and now these. I've had the chance to see just what V-Moda can do with their sounds.

The crossfade wireless is advertised, more or less, an M-100 with bluetooth and re-tuned drivers. Unfortunately, the only thing it truly retains from the M-100 is the way it looks.

Looking at the outside of the headphones, they're the same beautiful V-Moda crossfades that we've seen throughout their line--with buttons. The buttons look nice. They aren't obtrusive and they don't make you stand out like a lighthouse should you walk around with these in the middle of the night. The only light on the headphone is a fairly dim power light on the power switch. With that being said, I dislike the buttons. On the bottom of the headphone, we have the switch. Nothing wrong here, very sturdy feel to it. But at the top, we have the three buttons we will be using the most--Multi-Function (Play/Pause/Command), Volume up, and volume down. These three buttons feel flimsy to me and for worse, they are kind of hard to press, for some reason presenting resistance particularly when I try to turn the volume down. Perhaps they made it this way to avoid accidental pressing, but these buttons are right underneath the metal clip that holds the band to the cans so I'd imagine it would be somewhat difficult to bump into something that would hit the buttons here.

On the inside, we have a whole new story. If you're coming from the M-100, these are supposed to sound the same. Even after burn-in, the sound felt almost hollow to me, compared to the M-100. The bass was lacking, both on bluetooth and wireless, which is what most seem to buy V-Modas for. The mids were recessed, but this is no change from the M-100. The highs were also present, so no change here. Somewhere along the line, V-Moda tweaked these headphones and dropped (upped?) the bass from the M-100s. These headphones also lack aptX lossless/low-latency codec which is a major disappointment in this price range. The Sony MDR10BT has it and costs less. What gives, V-Moda?

The other thing to note in regards to the bluetooth is that if you listen to softer music, you may notice a near-silent static playing along with your music. This seems to be the standard for bluetooth headphones.

Other notes:
- The micro USB charging port is on the LEFT cup, while the 3.5mm plug is on the RIGHT cup. I prefer my wire on the left side, so this is entirely up to user preference.
- These lose the cliquefold mechanism that was so popular with the M-100. Bluetooth is intended for mobility, so it's strange that this would get removed, but it may be a design limitation here. If you're coming from the M-100, expect the larger LP case.
- These can be paired and connected with more than one device at a time, but can only play one at a time. This is pretty interesting, since the M-100s had two ports so that you could either listen to two sources at once or daisy chain your headphones. Unfortunately you can not stream to the cans and use the 3.5mm port as an audio-out.
- If you have the M-100s, or really any headphones that have a removable audio-in cable and want wireless, I'd check out these: [[ASIN:B0134DTP9Q BTunes VXB-35 (3.5mm Model) To Make Wired Headphones Wireless for Beats, Monster, Sony, V-Moda, Marshalls and more]]. I'm ended up returning my Crossfade Wireless and buying this instead.

review_text:
Excellent build quality. As the selling point of these suggest, these are in fact great when it comes to bass, they're not lying. However, the real selling point of these should be how well they're built. These headphones are the longest I've ever had a pair without them breaking. The only con in terms of build quality is the adhesive on the ear cushions started to decay, but some glue fixed that no problem. The big con, which isn't a con of the headphones themselves really, but because all these aux wires are made in China, they all fall apart absurdly fast. I go through 1 aux wire about every month or two, unless I get really lucky and get a decently made one (by China standards) that'll last a few months. I'm not being overly rough with them, I just use the headphones A LOT and the quality of the cables suck so, very easy to destroy them.

Now, over all audio quality. I'm picky about my audio quality. Picky enough where I can't stand not having an equalizer I can tweak to my liking, but I don't think it's quite fair to call myself an audiophile. That said, the over all audio quality seems fine to me. I did have a headset that was cheap, but supposed professionals were claiming they had really good audio quality despite the price. Comparing the two, I can tell a difference in audio, but not so much in quality. I couldn't tell you which ones sound better over all, I think it comes down more to preference unless you're doing super high end professional work where it's an absolute must to have sensitive headphones to pick apart audio at the seems. The main thing I seek in audio is heavy bass and these deliver, the non-bass audio sounds perfectly good too so over all I'm very happy.

I like these headphones enough that I ponied up for one of the expensive wireless upgraded versions of them, but if you're on somewhat of a low budget and these are available, I'd recommend them. Maybe I'm just lucky, but they should last a good while.

review_text:
Excellent build quality. As the selling point of these suggest, these are in fact great when it comes to bass, they're not lying. However, the real selling point of these should be how well they're built. These headphones are the longest I've ever had a pair without them breaking. The only con in terms of build quality is the adhesive on the ear cushions started to decay, but some glue fixed that no problem. The big con, which isn't a con of the headphones themselves really, but because all these aux wires are made in China, they all fall apart absurdly fast. I go through 1 aux wire about every month or two, unless I get really lucky and get a decently made one (by China standards) that'll last a few months. I'm not being overly rough with them, I just use the headphones A LOT and the quality of the cables suck so, very easy to destroy them.

Now, over all audio quality. I'm picky about my audio quality. Picky enough where I can't stand not having an equalizer I can tweak to my liking, but I don't think it's quite fair to call myself an audiophile. That said, the over all audio quality seems fine to me. I did have a headset that was cheap, but supposed professionals were claiming they had really good audio quality despite the price. Comparing the two, I can tell a difference in audio, but not so much in quality. I couldn't tell you which ones sound better over all, I think it comes down more to preference unless you're doing super high end professional work where it's an absolute must to have sensitive headphones to pick apart audio at the seems. The main thing I seek in audio is heavy bass and these deliver, the non-bass audio sounds perfectly good too so over all I'm very happy.

I like these headphones enough that I ponied up for one of the expensive wireless upgraded versions of them, but if you're on somewhat of a low budget and these are available, I'd recommend them. Maybe I'm just lucky, but they should last a good while.

review_text: Could not get it to work. I received my first Jabra HALO from DB Roth. It didn't work (I charged it with: 1. the hinges folded, 2. the hinges opened (like they would be if placed on one's head), 3. with hinges fully extended, each for two hours and did each of these charging iterations with 1. the earpieces extended and 2. the earpieces not extended for a total of 9 different charging iterations of two hours each). The charge indicator never indicated (it flashed on and off green on the LED charge indicator light, but never was solid green as the indicated in the instructions..after each charging iteration, I tried to turn the unit on and pair it with at least one Bluetooth device after each charging iteration). It never indicated that it was on, and never tried to pair with any of several Bluetooth devices automatically as indicated in the instructions. I tried automatic pairing with: 1. hinges opened, 2. hinges closed, each with ear pieces fully extended and with earpieces extended and closed. I never figured out how to turn it on and the Bluetooth indicator LED never indicated anything. I also tried to turn it on using the call button as indicated for manual paring in the instructions (note that the call button, the hinges, the volume control and the earpiece extensions are the only things that you can change on this headset so it is pretty easy to try all variations..none worked). During this process I depressed the call button for longer than 4 seconds numerous times, as well as less than 4 seconds numerous times and it did not try to pair with anything nor did it indicate that it was on at all. The Bluetooth light never indicated anyting (ever). I called Jabra Tech Support and they tried to help me by running me through several iterations of the process described in the instructions, but nothing that they told me to do worked (and I had already tried everything that was suggested (see above). The Tech Support representative concluded that the unit was defective and said to send it back to the seller (DB Roth). DB Roth replaced it with another unit promptly (I have to pay for shipping). The replacement unit acted the same exact way and I sent that back as well (had to pay for shipping again!). I even tried to use the hardwired input (mini USB with mini RCA jack plug in)and it would not work. I would really like to see how the HALO works and hear how it sounds, but I gave up trying to make either unit work and was tired of spending about $20 in shipping and numerous hours trying to get this thing to work. Life is too short for that. I am sure that, when the HALO works, it is a good Bluetooth headset, but I could not get it to work and I suspect that this seller is selling defective product..Conclusion: Avoid this seller and this product! Subsequently, I purchased the MOTO ROKR S305 (4 sets) and they all work great, sound great and fit my head more comfortably than the HALO. The MOTO ROKR costs considerably less than the HALO as well. I cannot comment on the ROKR vs. the HALO with regard to sound quality or utility with my iPhone as I could not get the HALO to work. To me, the choice here is a "no brainer"..MOTO ROKR all the way!

review_text: Could not get it to work. I received my first Jabra HALO from DB Roth. It didn't work (I charged it with: 1. the hinges folded, 2. the hinges opened (like they would be if placed on one's head), 3. with hinges fully extended, each for two hours and did each of these charging iterations with 1. the earpieces extended and 2. the earpieces not extended for a total of 9 different charging iterations of two hours each). The charge indicator never indicated (it flashed on and off green on the LED charge indicator light, but never was solid green as the indicated in the instructions..after each charging iteration, I tried to turn the unit on and pair it with at least one Bluetooth device after each charging iteration). It never indicated that it was on, and never tried to pair with any of several Bluetooth devices automatically as indicated in the instructions. I tried automatic pairing with: 1. hinges opened, 2. hinges closed, each with ear pieces fully extended and with earpieces extended and closed. I never figured out how to turn it on and the Bluetooth indicator LED never indicated anything. I also tried to turn it on using the call button as indicated for manual paring in the instructions (note that the call button, the hinges, the volume control and the earpiece extensions are the only things that you can change on this headset so it is pretty easy to try all variations..none worked). During this process I depressed the call button for longer than 4 seconds numerous times, as well as less than 4 seconds numerous times and it did not try to pair with anything nor did it indicate that it was on at all. The Bluetooth light never indicated anyting (ever). I called Jabra Tech Support and they tried to help me by running me through several iterations of the process described in the instructions, but nothing that they told me to do worked (and I had already tried everything that was suggested (see above). The Tech Support representative concluded that the unit was defective and said to send it back to the seller (DB Roth). DB Roth replaced it with another unit promptly (I have to pay for shipping). The replacement unit acted the same exact way and I sent that back as well (had to pay for shipping again!). I even tried to use the hardwired input (mini USB with mini RCA jack plug in)and it would not work. I would really like to see how the HALO works and hear how it sounds, but I gave up trying to make either unit work and was tired of spending about $20 in shipping and numerous hours trying to get this thing to work. Life is too short for that. I am sure that, when the HALO works, it is a good Bluetooth headset, but I could not get it to work and I suspect that this seller is selling defective product..Conclusion: Avoid this seller and this product! Subsequently, I purchased the MOTO ROKR S305 (4 sets) and they all work great, sound great and fit my head more comfortably than the HALO. The MOTO ROKR costs considerably less than the HALO as well. I cannot comment on the ROKR vs. the HALO with regard to sound quality or utility with my iPhone as I could not get the HALO to work. To me, the choice here is a "no brainer"..MOTO ROKR all the way!
